turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Stand behind — that's the bar. An agent is a machine: it keeps working after you stop touching it, and it builds exactly what you asked for, including the parts you didn't mean.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: So it isn't a tool that waits for my next keystroke. It runs, and it builds to spec — which means the spec is the thing I have to get right.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: And that's an old problem, not a new one. Every powerful tool has offered the same bargain: useless in careless hands, transformative in skilled ones.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: So for the first time, the limit on what I can build is my intent, not my hands.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: That skill is the whole prize. Operate the machine well and the labor moves to it while the judgment stays with you.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: The labor goes to the machine, the calls stay with me. That's the part I can't hand over.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: And that's the shape of the rest of the book. It starts on a foundation: know what you're actually running. See what the model can and can't do, and the pieces you assemble around it — everything after builds on that.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: So the foundation comes first, then three disciplines in order. The first: make the agent build what you meant. Hand over the goals, boundaries, and trade-offs it can't guess, so you get the file you expected rather than the one that merely seemed relevant.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: The second: trust results you can verify. Check the work with something other than the agent itself, because all checks passed isn't the same as the change I intended.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: And the third: own what ships. Set the bar before the code arrives, prove the work cleared it, and keep the final call your own.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: And the open-source part: everything here is something I can read, run, and change myself, with nobody steering the answers toward a product.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: Right. The book, the tools it references, and everything built around them are 100% open source, community-backed projects with no commercial agenda. No paid tiers, no enterprise licenses, nothing to buy.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: And the machine only pays off if you know what you're operating, so next is LLMs Demystified — the model itself, and what its behavior means for the work you hand it.
